episodes.157470: A slow moving and back building band of showers and thunderstorms produced early morning flash flooding in the Grapeland area of Houston County.
episodes.157482: Multiple waterspouts were sighted off the Galveston Island area.
episodes.157720: After several days of moist, low-level easterly flow across eastern New Mexico, that trend finally diminished as winds across the area became more variable. With an area of high pressure building over the Rockies, drier air began to filter into the area which lessened storm coverage on June 1, 2021. Still, enough moisture and instability continued to allow for thunderstorms with isolated severe thunderstorms for areas along and east of the central mountain chain. The strongest thunderstorms for the day were located across south central and east central New Mexico where nickel to quarter size hail was reported. Minor home damage was also reported in Dilia with the large hail.
episodes.157771: A severe thunderstorm produced hail up to golfball size just east of Fort Morgan.  The hail smashed a windshield.
episodes.157793: Widespread heavy rainfall that fell across the Neches River basin of East Texas during May, and particularly on May 31st, which resulted in a secondary significant rise on the Neches River west of Alto to above major flood stage during the first several days of June.
episodes.157918: A shower moving along the coast produced a short-lived waterspout near Indian Harbour Beach in Brevard County.
episodes.157996: A pre-frontal trough and upper level disturbance triggered severe thunderstorms across the coastal waters.
episodes.158344: A slow moving cold front interacted with a very warm and moist airmass across the region and produced very heavy rainfall mainly along and north of I20.  About 2 to 4 inches fell mainly along and north of a line from Sterling City to Brownwood and flooded several roads across the region.
episodes.158409: Up to 7 inches of rain fell in less than two hours in Port Orange during an isolated thunderstorm, resulting in some temporary roadway flooding.
episodes.158780: Deep easterly flow allowed for ample moisture to advect into South Florida. This moisture, combined with an upper level low centered over the northern Bahamas resulted in scattered showers and thunderstorms to develop. A few strong storms over the Atlantic  waters produced gusty winds and waterspouts.
episodes.158782: Deep easterly flow allowed for ample moisture to advect into South Florida. This moisture, combined with an upper level low centered over the northern Bahamas resulted in scattered showers and thunderstorms to develop. A strong storm that moved over Palm Beach County produced a funnel cloud.
episodes.158794: An upper trough was over the region with abundant low-level moisture present across West Texas. A cold front was moving southward from southwest Oklahoma and there was a nearly stationary outflow boundary across Ector County from storms the previous day. Rain and thunderstorms were across the Permian Basin during the morning hours which resulted in hail across portions of the area. High instability due to clearing skies allowed for severe thunderstorms to develop across the southern Permian Basin and in Pecos County during the afternoon hours. These storms produced large hail and tornadoes. Flash flooding developed across portions of the Permian Basin during the early afternoon hours.
episodes.158882: A weakening line of thunderstorms Memorial Day morning, followed by a second line of storms that evening (which developed along an approaching cold front), led to instances of heavy rain and flooding across the region. One storm also produced minor wind damage.
episodes.158928: A cold front generated thunderstorms as it moved through South Central Texas. One of these storms produced large hail.
episodes.159146: Heavy rain in early June brought flooding to several rivers in central and northeast Arkansas.
episodes.159305: A cold front generated thunderstorms as it moved through South Central Texas. One of these storms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding.
episodes.159464: A cold front helped to ignite thunderstorm development across south-central Texas early on June 1st. Outflow boundaries from this activity allowed for additional storms to develop across Deep South Texas and the Rio Grande Valley. Heavy rain occurred across the Lower Rio Grande Valley, which led to several instances of minor street flooding in the McAllen Metro region.
episodes.159892: A squall line of thunderstorms formed over the Brush Country during the early morning hours of June 1st. The squall line reached the Coastal Bend and the nearby coastal water around daybreak. Wind gusts between 35 and 40 knots occurred between Corpus Christi Bay and Baffin Bay.
episodes.160074: The setup was not overly favorable for widespread severe weather on this day, however, isolated thunderstorms did develop across the eastern plains of Colorado. A few severe storms did develop, and produced hail to one inch across Pueblo and Kiowa counties.
episodes.160109: During the late afternoon a couple groups of thunderstorms progressed east from Colorado into Northwest Kansas.  The thunderstorms produced hail up to penny in size.
episodes.160350: An elongated trough extended from the Northern Plains into Southeast Arizona.  Temperatures warmed into the lower 90s near the Arizona border with dew points near 30 providing an atmosphere for gusty thunderstorm outflows.
episodes.160622: An isolated waterspout develop in association with a developing rain shower just offshore Key Largo. A well-defined upper-level low pressure system was noted east of southeast Florida, and the airmass was moist with very little convective inhibition.

events.narrative: Amateur radio reported multiple vehicles stranded in flooded roadways near Dallas Executive Airport.
A National Weather Service employee reported flash flooding along FM 1886 at Silver Creek, with water rushing over the road.
FM 576 was closed due to high water; but the exact location and extent of the closure was not confirmed.
Street flooding occurred in Coolidge. Some of the water spilled over and inundated house yards.
FM 57 was closed due to flooding.
There was water in homes and street flooding was reported in Hamlin.  Also FM 1661, FM 126 and FM 57 were closed in Jones County due to flooding.
A public report indicated a downed tree and minor flooding near the intersection of Highway 79 and Highway 294.

Widespread rainfall amounts of fifteen to in excess of twenty inches fell across the Neches River basin of East Texas during May, including three to in excess of eight inches that fell May 31st. As a result, a secondary crest occurred on the Neches River southwest of Alto near Highway 21, rising back above the 18 foot moderate flood stage at 1215 pm on June 1st, surpassing the 20 foot major flood stage at 315 pm on the 1st, before cresting at 20.3 feet at 8 pm that evening. A sharp recession occurred afterwards, with the river falling below 20 feet at 730 am on June 2nd, and below 18 feet at 8 am on the 4th. This flooding resulted in moderate to severe flooding of the heavily wooded floodplain, with boat ramps and picnic areas completely inundated.
Flooding continued into early June on the White River at Augusta.
Flooding continued into early June on the White River at Clarendon.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding. Water completely covered El Indio Hwy in Eagle Pass. Several vehicles were stranded with water up to their bumpers.

Heavy rains produce flash flooding in and around the Grapeland area. A water rescue was performed along FM 228 approximately two miles east of Grapeland after a car was swept off the road by floodwaters.
Flash flooding caused a washout in one lane of FM 2423 between County Road 1840 and US Highway 287 North.

Several weather spotters and mesonet stations recorded rainfall of 3 to over 7 inches in less than two hours. Roadways were flooded with stalled cars on S. Williamson Boulevard, south of Taylor Road in Port Orange.
A member of the public shared a photo of a funnel cloud from a strong thunderstorm that formed west of Lion Country Safari and south of US 98.
